question: Purushottam Dadheech is a famous and recognised Indian __________ dancer.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Purushottam Dadheech is a renowned exponent of the Kathak dance form, one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
 
• He has been instrumental in promoting Kathak through his performances, teachings, and scholarly works.
 
• Dadheech has received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to Kathak, including the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.
 
• He is known for his deep understanding and innovative approach to the traditional form of Kathak, blending it with contemporary elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance Form:**

 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form that originated in northern India, characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha," meaning story, and "Kathakar," meaning storyteller.
 
• It is traditionally performed by solo dancers, but group performances have also become popular.
 
• Kathak has three main gharanas (schools) - Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras, each with its distinct style and repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award:**
 
 
• It is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists for their outstanding contribution to the performing arts.
 
• The award includes a cash prize, a citation, and a shawl.
 
• It was established in 1952 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu)
 
• Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh)
 
• Odissi (Odisha)
 
• Manipuri (Manipur)
 
• Mohiniyattam (Kerala)
 
• Sattriya (Assam)
 
 
 
• **Gharanas in Kathak:**
 
 
• **Lucknow Gharana:** Known for its grace, elegance, and expressive emotions.
 
• **Jaipur Gharana:** Emphasizes powerful footwork and extensive use of space.
 
• **Banaras Gharana:** Combines elements of both Lucknow and Jaipur styles, known for its unique compositions and rhythmic patterns.
